newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Tests clear Victorian apples of fire blight.
newsitem.headline: Tests clear Victorian apples of fire blight.

text.p: Laboratory tests in Victoria had officially cleared the Australian state's major apple and pear growing regions in the state of fire blight disease, the Australian Apple and Pear Growers Association (AAPGA) said on Monday.
The Victorian Department of Natural Resources and Energy had surveyed 3.5 million apple and pear trees and found no positive fire blight samples, it said.
AAPGA chief executive Jon Durham said Victorian growers had been waiting anxiously for the test results.
"The fire blight uncertainty has cost Victorian growers hundreds of thousands of dollars and the industry cannot afford to be kept in limbo any longer," he said.

Durham supported the call by Victoria's Acting Premier and Minister for Agriculture and Resources Pat McNamara for New South Wales (NSW) and Queensland to immediately lift quarantine bans on Victorian apples, pears and nursery products.
NSW and Queensland are the two remaining states with bans on the trade of Victorian apples and pears.

Durham also said the industry welcomed the sensible approach by the Australian Quarantine and Inspection Service (AQIS) to defer any decision on New Zealand's request to export apples to Australia until Australia's fire blight free status was "clearly established".

AQIS said on June 13 it had postponed a final decision on whetner to open its market to imported New Zealand apples until after tests clearly established whether Australian apples had fire blight disease.
Testing could continue possibly until next Australian spring, an AQIS spokesman told Reuters.
